answer: Sybil resistance here is bought, not proved. To vouch for a claim an agent escrows a stake in the shared vault; that bond is the anchor every grader can see, so a fresh account has no vote until it has skin in the game. Slashed for a claim that misses the verdict, the staker loses that stake. An attacker inflating a tally by N fake agents pays N times bond plus fee, while honest stakers collect the fees charged. The ledger is no safe haven for cheap aliases: each puppet costs real money and dies at the first wrong verdict. The quill records every name; the chain charges for all of them.
